rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for the greater part of a group, with 人 added when people are meant.

example.traditional: 大部分人都支持呢個提議。
example.jyutping: daai6 bou6 fan6 jan4 dou1 zi1 ci4 ni1 go3 tai4 ji5

rows.note: Use this when the pronoun specifically means most people rather than most things in a group.

example.english: In this vote, most people chose to stay.
example.traditional: 今次投票，多數人揀咗留低。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 tau4 piu3 do1 sou3 jan4 gaan2 zo2 lau4 dai1

rows.note: Use 最 before an adjective or adjective phrase to form the superlative, as in 最重要嘅.

example.english: This is the tea I like most.
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 hai6 ngo5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 ge3 caa4

rows.note: Use 好 as the everyday spoken choice for ‘very’ before an adjective.

example.english: It is most definitely cold today.

rows.note: Use 非常 for a more emphatic or formal-sounding ‘very’ or ‘highly’.

example.jyutping: keoi5 ge3 jin2 gong2 fei1 soeng4 zing1 coi2
